No, that is not true. The Swiss Confederation did not adopt its first constitution in 1291, and it has certainly changed over time. The origins of the Swiss Confederation date back to 1291, when the cantons of Uri, Schwyz, and Unterwalden formed an alliance. However, the first written constitution, known as the Federal Charter of 1291, was not a formal constitution in the modern sense but rather a pact among the cantons.

The modern Swiss Constitution was adopted in 1848, and it has been revised several times since then, most recently in 2000. Therefore, the statement that the Swiss Confederation adopted its first constitution in 1291, which remains unchanged to this day, is incorrect.
